page: OVHcloud a10-90 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 60 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9554 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 85.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.42 GB per core. For acceleration, the server is equipped with two NVIDIA A10 GPUs from the Ampere family, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-core performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25%. The memory subsystem demonstrates top-tier cached read bandwidth and strong uncached write speeds, though uncached read bandwidth remains average. In LLM inference benchmarks, the dual NVIDIA A10 configuration achieves top-tier performance across small, medium, and large models, demonstrating high token-per-second throughput for both prompt processing and text generation.

This server offers high resource density by combining 60 dedicated physical CPU cores with dual enterprise GPUs, making it a cost-efficient option for parallel processing workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. However, the relatively low memory-to-core ratio of 1.42 GB per core represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications. The hardware profile is optimized for large language model inference, multi-threaded data processing, ray tracing, and GPU-accelerated machine learning workloads.
